writeup: TIC 394805902 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 8.1303 days. Automated analysis of TESS photometry revealed a primary eclipse causing 9.25% dimming, along with a secondary eclipse detected at 7.7 sigma significance occurring at orbital phase 0.41. The binary's light curve shows a remarkably strong detection signal with a Box Least Squares signal-to-noise ratio of 936.6. Pixel-level image analysis confirmed the signal, detecting a centroid offset of 2.1 arcsec from the target location with a peak signal-to-noise of 49.7. The candidate does not appear in any of six major variable-star catalogs, and passed all automated data quality checks. With a machine-learning screening score of 0.79, this system represents a potentially valuable addition to known eclipsing binaries.
